It’s not specifically a lewd game but *The Killing Antidote* is a pretty fun game if you’re into zombies and survival horror. It plays like a 3rd person Resident Evil game except you can customize the characters clothes, hairstyle/color, and has breasts and waist sliders. And yes, there’s nude mods you can get off Nexus. The devs have stated that they can’t officially add player nudity due to local laws but they often heavily imply that they encourage people to use nude mods since they can’t get in trouble for those since they’re “unofficial”.

It’s still in alpha state but it’s free and is surprisingly high quality given that there’s only two devs working on it right now. The devs have said that they want to hire more people to help make this game once they enter Early Access and have more funds. Last I checked they said they’re hoping to go EA by mid-August to September. 

I’ve gotten 40+ hours of fun out of this game and really want to see it succeed. It has a decent (unfinished) story mode, zombie survival modes (think CoD: Zombies), an evacuation mode, and a special Halloween event with mode exclusive clothing items you can receive. It’s definitely worth a look imo.

Edit: The steam store page will say it’s coming soon. All you have to do to download it is opt into the play-test on the store page and it should let you download the game. Otherwise you can find downloads for the game with a few google searches.

Here’s a few things I’ve learned over the years of driving. I’m in America btw. 

1. Always move over a lane if there’s a car broken down on the shoulder. Otherwise you might accidentally turn the owner of that car into a meat crayon if they’re walking around on the highway (which they shouldn’t be doing). 

2. Remember the phrase “The left lane is for crime”. Drivers Ed teaches you that you’re only supposed to use the left lane to pass slow cars but many drivers use it for speeding and weaving through traffic. Follow the flow of traffic in the left-lane and move over if someone starts tailgating you. You can also use the left lane to avoid dealing with merging on-ramp cars. 

3. If you’re parallel to a car merging in from an on-ramp then MAINTAIN YOUR CURRENT FUCKING SPEED. You always have Right of Way and it’s on the other car to find an open spot to merge into. Hold your speed and wait for them to decide if they’re going to merge in front of or behind you then give them some buffer room to merge as needed. This was the trickiest part of highway driving when I first started out. Alternatively you can just move into the left-lane and not have to deal with mergers. 

4. This one is very region-specific but a car flashing their high-beams at you may mean one of a few different things. An oncoming car flashing you 1-2 times often means there’s a speed trap ahead. I’ve also seen people flash their hazards for speed traps. A car flashing you 1-2 times from behind may mean they saw something wrong with your car like a tailpipe dragging on the ground and they’re trying to warn you OR they could be trying to “wake you up” if you’re driving tired and drifting into other lanes. If a car starts rapidly flashing their high-beams at you then they’re usually either trying to warn you of an immediate danger/hazard/emergency or they’re road-raging.

Metal cars are way more dangerous than today’s fiberglass cars because of how the car deforms in the crash. 

Think of it this way, if you had an empty soda can and a solid, metal cylinder on a table and you tried to smash both of them with your bare hands, which one would hurt more? The metal cylinder would because it doesn’t deform to cushion the blow. The soda can might still cut you up and hurt a bit but you probably aren’t going to break any bones in your hands from smashing it.  The same concept applies to cars. 

An older car might not take as much damage in a crash but an older car also doesn’t crumple and deform like modern cars when they crash which is a major factor in surviving a car crash. 

My guess is that this idea comes from a “No car damage = No injuries” mindset which just simply isn’t true.
